item.title: Patch 9.0.4
item.description:
Hey folks,

We’ve just rolled out Patch 9.0.4 to Total War: WARHAMMER III, with a particular focus on optimising Nagash’s campaign experience, alongside various other fixes and adjustments across the board. You can read the full Patch Notes below, with Nagash-related items detailed in their own section, followed by all other changes.

As always, if you run into any new issues after updating the 9.0.4, please raise them over in our dedication bug reporting sub-forum. Please include as much information as you’re able to within your report, including screenshots and save files (mod-free if possible, or let us know in the report if you use mods), as this greatly helps us in our investigations.

Our intention is to have a 9.0.5 release within the next few weeks which, alongside various fixes and adjustments, should include some improvements to Victory Objectives with the goal of making them more relevant and impactful.

Until then, we’ll see you on the battlefield!

— The Total War Team

Nagash

Campaign
General/Gameplay

  • Expanded the search functionality in The Black Pyramid to now also match the names of specific units contained within unit sets and other hover-over text.

  • Fixed an issue when playing as Nagash where a fort settlement obtained via confederation or diplomacy had the wrong settlement type and main building.

  • Fixed an issue where the ‘Sun-Scorched, Sand-Blistered’ node on the Black Pyramid was not applying flaming attacks to Ushabti (Great Bows), Horse Archers & Horse Chariots.

  • Fixed a Grave Call unlocking node in the Black Pyramid which was incorrectly giving access to the wrong units.

  • Fixed an issue where the Lahmian Halls and Halls of Glories Past would lock again for Nagash after loading a save, even if Neferata and Walach had previously been subjugated.

  • When playing as Nagash, fighting battles in a region that is not part of Land of the Dead now shows a warning icon that no Necromantic Energy is granted from battles in that region.

  • Fixed an issue where Necromantic Energy from battles was not being awarded if the battle was fought in a region with an abandoned settlement.

  • Nagash's building effects that are enabled by devastation now take effect immediately instead of in the next turn.

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash's gold resource buildings weren't granting their Lord recruit rank bonus when replacing an existing Lord.

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash's landmark in the Black Pyramid of Nagash was granting 1 additional Lord recruit rank than it should when replacing Lords rather than recruiting new Lords.

  • Fixed an issue where the Nameless would remain on the Campaign map after their death during Crisis Mode events.

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash was able to recruit Regiments of Renown outside of his owned territories.

  • Fixed an issue where some of Luthor Harkon's ship buildings were not working after being confederated by Nagash.

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash’s Necropolis tutorial could function incorrectly when Hotkeys are pressed.

  • Fixed an issue where transferring a Book of Nagash could not work correctly in some sea regions and open seas.

Skills, Abilities & Traits

  • Adjusted Pinnacle of Servitude skill for Nagash, reducing its Recruit Rank bonus to 1, but allowing it to also apply to units recruited via Grave Call.

  • Fixed an issue where the Black Pyramid Sigil "Named to Protect" could cause Heroes to gain multiple stacks of the Guardian ability.

Items & Ancillaries

  • Fixed an issue where Isabella was unable to reequip the Blood Chalice of Bathori if unequipped after confederating Sylvania as Nagash.

UI

  • Fixed an issue where The Great Blades Unsheathed node in the Black Pyramid was displaying the wrong effect icon.

  • Fixed an issue where the available sigils UI in the Black Pyramid was not returning to the correct position after spending or refunding a sigil, resulting in it being positioned slightly off-screen.

  • Nagash’s Grave Call Recruitment button is now greyed-out when unavailable. Additionally, we have added a tooltip explaining that it is only available in Land of the Dead.

  • Fixed an issue when playing as Nagash where some buildings could show as Ruined in landmark building chains.

  • Fixed an issue where Subjugating the Nameless or some of the other Legendary Hero Mortarchs could show the wrong text.

  • Fixed an issue when playing as Nagash where the Encamp army stance incorrectly mentioned Global recruitment.

  • Fixed an issue where some tooltips that grant extra ability uses in the Black Pyramid panel were missing details of that ability.

  • Attempting to Occupy, Colonise or Resettle a region as a Necropolis now indicates if the Necropolis limit will be exceeded as a result.

  • Fixed an issue where some mission objectives in the Mortarchs panel were lacking a button to zoom to the relevant location for that objective.

  • Fixed an issue where Dieter Helsnicht's "The Silent Legion" requirement text exceeded the dimensions of the text box.

  • Fixed an issue where the Sigil Browser in The Black Pyramid would overlap the Shambling Hordes cluster of nodes when fully zoomed out at some resolutions and UI scaling options.

  • Fixed an issue where an empty tooltip would show for some factions when hovering over a Book of Nagash that another army was carrying.

  • Clicking on the Land of the Dead panel name now opens a help page about the Land of the Dead within the Province panel, as with other settlements.

  • The settlement requirements text for the Ritual of Undeath no longer appears after the Ritual of Undeath has been enacted.

  • Fixed an issue where the "Disempower Sigils" button in The Black Pyramid would be active even when no Sigils are currently Empowered.

  • Fixed an issue where spells granted to Nagash by Awakening the power of a Book of Nagash showed a different number of uses in his character details panel than in the Books of Nagash panel.

  • Removed progress bars from the Mortarch mission objectives to make the panel UI more consistent.

VFX

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash’s persistent VFX would linger in another character’s ‘Character Detail’ view when clicking between two characters.

  • Fixed an issue where the VFX could flicker in some character details portholes, including Nagash.

Battle
Maps

  • The Khemri siege battle map now features the Black Pyramid of Nagash looming over the city.

Spells & Abilities

  • Fixed an issue where the Book of Nagash spell ‘Incantation of the Skullstorm’ would incorrectly target the area behind the unit that needs to be targeted.

  • Reduced the trigger time for Screaming Skull Catapults' homing ability, granted by the Black Pyramid ‘Seeker of Kindred Skulls’ node, from 3s to 2s.

VFX

  • Fixed an issue where moving Nagash to a new position during the deployment phase would leave lingering VFX in his previous location.

Multiplayer

  • Nagash buildings locked behind subjugations will now be unlocked if Neferata or Walach start or become owned by a co-op partner in multiplayer campaigns.

  • Fixed an issue where Nagash's buildings locked behind subjugation remained locked if Neferata or Walach start or become owned by a co-op partner.

Additional Release Notes

Performance & Stability

  • Fixed a crash that could occur after ending the turn during the Nagash End Times crisis.

  • Fixed an issue where the game could freeze for a long period of time during very late game turn ends.

Campaign
General/Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, after the Chaos Invasion Endgame had concluded, a razed region colonised by a faction would become unoccupiable by any factions subsequently conquering that region.

  • Fixed an issue where the player was unable to construct the port building in the Altar of the Horned Rat after capturing it from the Vermintide faction. (Please note that this will only affect new campaigns.)

  • Fixed an issue where The Liche High Priest (Nehekhara) was unable to correctly unlock Arcane Conduit.

  • Storm attrition generated by a player-spawned storm no longer affects the player’s armies or those of allied factions.

  • Fixed an issue where Short Victory rewards that decrease the cost of Bloodlines rituals were not being applied correctly.

  • Fixed an issue where the Altdorf College of Forbidden Magic landmark was incorrectly providing double the amount of Winds Of Magic power reserve per turn.

  • Fixed an issue where some characters no longer had a background Trait after their faction is confederated.

  • In the Great-Smart plans, when attempting a Verminlord summon, you can now see for each selection the base Verminlord's unit card from the Verminlord that will be summoned if successful.

  • When attempting a Verminlord summon in the Great-Smart plans panel, each option now displays the base Verminlord’s unit card that will be summoned if successful.

  • Fixed an issue where the Enforce Confederation option for Warriors of Chaos was incorrectly vassalising instead of properly confederating.

  • Fixed an issue where Styrkaar’s mission was triggering for all factions instead of only Slaanesh, Warriors of Chaos and Norsca.

  • Fixed an issue where some Lords could lose access to some of their mounts after being confederated. (Please note that this will only affect new campaigns.)

Skills, Abilities & Traits

  • Fixed an issue where Arkhan's skill ‘Legions of Death’ was not affecting Chillgheists.

UI

  • Fixed an issue where the Vampire Counts confederation requirement for the target faction to have no more than 5 regions was not displayed.

  • Fixed some inconsistencies with scrolling behaviour within the unit recruitment panel.

  • Added missing localisations for text strings introduced in 9.0.3.

VFX

  • Fixed an issue where a character that has lost The Nemesis Crown could still have the VFX as if they were still carrying it.

Battle
Spells & Abilities

  • Reduced the duration of the ‘Soul Slaying Hunger’ ability to more accurately match the Visual Effect duration.

  • Reduced the radius of ‘Mist Form’ ability to more accurately match the Visual Effect and targeting area.

  • Fixed an issue where Invocation of Nehek could be cast on units that have reached their healing cap in battle.

Multiplayer

  • Added the ability for the host of a Multiplayer lobby to see and adjust the AI Anti-Player Bias slider.

⚠ IMPORTANT

If you experience any issues after downloading the update, please take a moment to Verify the integrity of the game files first to ensure there were no issues when downloading. A step-by-step guide can be found in this article. If the issues persist, please visit our support site for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

🧱 MOD WARNING

Please note that user-generated mods may have compatibility issues with new game updates. If you are encountering performance or stability issues following a release, is recommended that you disable any mods you're running. If you continue to experience issues, please visit our support site for additional troubleshooting steps and assistance.

item.title: Zealot Archetype: In the Name of the God-Emperor
item.description:
Service to the God-Emperor takes many forms. Among the denizens of the Imperium, there are those who devote their lives not only to spreading His word, but to personally delivering His wrath as well.

Meet the Zealot — a new melee-focused first-tier archetype that makes their debut in the Processional of the Damned DLC. A powerful short-range combatant, the Zealot combines an arsenal of area-of-effect attacks with great effectiveness in drawing the attention of the enemy.

The new companion, Stella, belongs to this archetype, but the Zealot is not exclusive to her — this option will also be available to the Lord Captain at character creation.

After all, a Rogue Trader is one of the most powerful conduits of His will!



Up Close and Personal

The Zealot’s niche on the battlefield is that of a splash-damage fighter/off-tank who prefers operating close to enemy lines, drawing attention with a reliable taunt mechanic.

This archetype utilises maces, hammers and other brutal bludgeoning weapons. Yet the Zealot is not limited exclusively to melee combat — their arsenal also includes more exotic options, such as swinging weapons bound to chains or even hurling them at the enemy.

The Zealot’s primary stats are Weapon Skill, Strength, Toughness and Willpower, and their abilities scale with Athletics, Carouse, Lore (Imperium), Lore (Warp) and Lore (Xenos). In fact, Lore skills will directly affect how much damage is inflicted on the appropriate enemy category — talk about knowing your enemy!

On the second tier, Zealot may advance into Vanguard, Archmilitant, Master Tactician, or Executioner, further amplifying their defensive and offensive capabilities.


Wrath of the God-Emperor

The first keystone ability of the Zealot, Thunderous Echo, is a special passive effect applied to any attacks made with bludgeoning weapons, adding an area-of-effect modifier to them.

With this effect, all enemies and allies within one additional tile of the weapon’s normal attack pattern take additional damage, with the amount of damage scaling differently for one-handed and two-handed weapons. The damage is also doubled on prone targets.

The image below showcases the pattern:


This ability provides the Zealot with an excellent tool for dealing with hordes of weaker enemies or applying negative effects to multiple targets at once. Talents may further increase the affected area or modify its shape and damage.

But be wary of friendly fire — your allies will also suffer damage if they end up in the afflicted area!

Judgement From Afar

The Zealot’s second, and arguably even more exciting, keystone ability is called the Zealous Throw:

The Zealot throws their weapon into the target cell, dealing weapon damage to the first creature in its path. All creatures around the target receive additional damage from Thunderous Echo. The weapon then returns to the Zealot’s hand. Works only with bludgeoning weapons.

This ability does not count towards the attack limit per turn and can be further enhanced by a number of talents, including the option to throw two one-handed weapons at once.

Who said hammers and maces were not ranged weapons, anyway?



Let Them Come

Unlike Blade Dancer from the Void Shadows DLC, the Zealot does not boast exceptional mobility. Instead, they prefer to let the enemy get up close, with two distinct tools for making them do so:

1) The third keystone ability called Ardour, which costs 1 AP to activate:

For 1 round, all enemies that were dealt damage by the Zealot consider them a priority target. All incoming damage dealt to the Zealot is decreased by (Carouse / 10)% per affected target.

2) An archetype ability called Sacrifice Thyself:

The Zealot makes a religious cry in a radius equal to (WIL Bonus) cells around them. Enemies in the radius must pass a WIL Test (-Zealot's level) or move as close as possible to the Zealot.
Daemons fail this Test automatically.

This gives the Zealot a significant degree of control over the distribution of incoming damage, making them a reliable tank indeed. They may not be as sturdy as Abelard at first, but combined with late-game abilities from their second-tier archetypes, they can become a force to be reckoned with.

Break the Chains

What about Heroic Acts and Desperate measures? Let’s have a look at them as well:

The Zealot’s Heroic Act is called the Unchained Punishment:

Until the end of the turn, the Zealot starts spinning their chained bludgeoning weapon and gains (WIL Bonus) stacks of Unchained Punishment. After moving into an adjacent cell, they consume 1 stack and deal 50% weapon damage to all enemies within 1 cell. These strikes trigger Thunderous Echo. Upon activation, the Zealot automatically deals damage to all enemies within 1 cell, while not consuming any stacks. Once all stacks are consumed, the Zealot continues moving as usual.

With a two-handed weapon, strikes deal (WS Bonus) additional damage. With a weapon in each hand, the Zealot strikes twice per cell traversed.

Removes Immobilized. Until all stacks of Unchained Punishment are consumed, the Zealot cannot change their weapon set. While moving, the Zealot does not trigger attacks of opportunity.

The Desperate Measure version of this ability adds the following downsides:

The Zealot receives Direct damage equal to 5% of their maximum Wounds per cell traversed.
After the turn ends and until the end of the combat, the Zealot's max MP are decreased to (WIL Bonus).

Upgrades to these abilities include additional damage, a pushback effect, and increased block chance and protection from the damage done to allies.

Time to dust off your thunder hammer, Lord Captain!





More Details

The archetype has several other area-of-effect abilities and is supplemented by a plethora of talents and new items designed for it. These include modifications and boosts to damage, mobility, tanking options, attack range, attack pattern size, pushback, additional negative effects on inflicting damage, and much more.

While we won’t go into each and every one of them for now, the Zealot archetype will offer a rich variety of build options.

And of course, let’s not forget the synergy this archetype is designed to have with Stella’s origin — the Miraculist. The combination of their abilities opens up a wide range of different playstyles.



That is all for today, but stay tuned for more exciting details about the Processional of the Damned.

The God-Emperor protects!

--

The God-Emperor protects!

item.title: Feature Highlight: Prophet of Decay Enemy Design
item.description:
The new free update for Warhammer 40,000: Darktide, Depths of the Damned, comes loaded with new content for the game! Including a new mission, live story, weapons and boss fight.

In today’s Feature Highlight, we’ve interviewed our Enemy Designer Jonathan about the work that went into making the boss fight at the end of the new Spillway mission. 

For those who have not played it yet, be wary of spoilers! This Feature Highlight will very candidly speak about how the boss plays and the story involved!

“My name is Jonathan. I work on Darktide and I’m the Enemy / Pacing Designer, so I’m a part of creating all the enemies and maintaining the Enemy Director of the game, primarily.” ~ Jonathan

Initial Design
A new boss enemy

We decided pretty early into development that we wanted to have a unique boss for the end event of the mission, and there were two main reasons for it. One is simply that we thought it’d be cool to make a new unique boss, since we haven’t introduced one since the Karnak Twins, and that this mission was a good opportunity to do that.

But on top of that, we’ve also been itching to introduce a Psyker enemy for a while, and whilst exploring different options of how to introduce one, we realized that a boss is a great way to do it.

“A Psyker is a very good medium for making a boss-type encounter since you can do a lot of warp stuff, which allows you a greater versatility and mobility in what you do with a boss. Especially compared to something that is melee, which is more limiting.” ~ Jonathan

We really wanted to play up the Psyker aspects of the fight, especially a Psyker of Nurgle, by emphasizing a lack of physicality in how he fights. This idea guided the design of not just how the Prophet attacks but also how he moves!

“He turns into flies and then, well, flies to wherever he wants to go. He doesn’t move anymore.” ~ Jonathan

Campaign and Adventure

As you saw when playing the mission (you DID play the mission, right?), the Prophet of Decay boss is none other than Rodin Karnak! The ritual has allowed him to take over a new body, bloated and rotten with Nurgle’s generous blessing, and with new Psyker abilities. (Though still voiced by the same talented voice actor as ever: Jack Myers) 

The Spillway mission is part of the new mini campaign “Terrors of the Deep”, and while the campaign version of the mission represents the first time that Rodin has shown himself since the Dark Communion, players will still get to fight him again and again whenever they pick Spillway from the regular mission board. As he himself points out during the mission’s end cinematic, it is not so easy to get rid of one blessed by Nurgle as he is…

“It’s definitely going to be part of the normal mission pool, and also in Havoc, of course. And in Havoc, you know, it’s gonna be hard. There’s gonna be some additional stuff happening that might not happen in other difficulties.” ~ Jonathan

Gameplay Design - Fighting the Prophet of Decay

One of the biggest inspirations for how the Prophet of Decay bossfight functions is actually from Vermintide 2! Specifically Nurgloth the Eternal, the Lord fight at the end of Enchanter’s Lair, which was part of the Curse of Drachenfels campaign. The damaging ring mechanics, for instance, or the way the bosses use projectiles, were both heavily inspired by him.

“The first phase is the rings, similar to Nurgloth, ‘cause I always thought that they were a very cool mechanic and they work very well. Since a boss in a game like Darktide has to work in first person \[...] so we can’t do too crazy stuff, since you can’t look behind you. There’s a lot of, like, restrictions that makes a boss in Darktide something different compared to other games.” ~ Jonathan

Compared to Darktide’s other bossfights, this one is very structured, having three phases that players go through as they damage the Prophet as well as a very hand crafted pacing that controls things such as the boss getting winded and stopping for a moment while hordes of enemies swarm down, etc.

“It’s more of what you could call a ‘raid boss’ in other games.” ~ Jonathan

The first phase we settled on quite quickly, but the second and third phase required a lot more iteration; trying different ideas, testing them out, seeing what works and what doesn’t, polishing them and so on until finally landing on the version that went live with the Depths of the Damned update. An example of a scrapped idea was to have Phase 2 be about standing in specific spots and getting launched into the air if you failed to get to safety in time!

“\[...] it is very hard to keep track of multiple focus points during the course of a fight. You have to focus on \[the Boss], you have to focus on the normal enemies, but then you would also have to focus on a third element. So we had to ensure that that third element is \[...] noticeable enough that you can see it in your peripheral vision.” ~ Jonathan

Coming up with challenging, unique mechanics for the boss fight while working within the constraints that the limited field of view of a First Person perspective imposes was half of the challenge. Once we had a solid foundation for how the boss fight structure is, came the second half, which was fine tuning all of the elements to work together and make the final result, the entire fight itself, be a satisfying experience.

“\[...] like, sure, you can make phases, you can make all of these mechanics, but unless you can make them work together in a cohesive manner, it’s not gonna feel good to play even if on a technical level it works.” ~ Jonathan

Things like how long should each phase take on average, how that changes per difficulty (from Uprising to Havoc 40), or even how to gate each phase. These all contribute to getting the feel of the fight just right.

Another detail that required a lot of fine tuning were the additional enemies that would swarm the players during the fight. They’re half of the fight by themselves, after all! For example, the ‘intermission’ sections where the Prophet is unable to attack are the only moments of the boss fight where ranged enemies may spawn. 

In all other situations, only melee enemies can spawn, since dealing with the Prophet, the hazards he spawns, his projectiles and ranged enemies proved to be too much.

“That being said, the type of melee enemies are dependent on the difficulty you’re playing. \[...] If you’re playing on lower difficulties you’re only going to get Poxwalkers and other chaff-type enemies. But if you play on Damnation and up, you’re going to get Elites, including Ogryn enemies.” ~ Jonathan

On the subject of difficulty, the method we usually use for adjusting difficulty is to first pick a base difficulty, fine tune everything for that, and then adjust up and down for the difficulties near it. In this case, we actually had two bases to work from. The fight was fine tuned for Malice and Auric. The Uprising version was then based on the Malice baseline, while Damnation and Heresy were based on the Auric baseline.

Development Challenges

The Prophet of Decay is a very unique encounter, and many of the mechanics it uses required developing entirely new systems to handle them. Something as simple as having projectiles that can be broken by player attacks required a lot of work, because it wasn’t something that had been done in Darktide yet. In the second phase of the fight, players are encouraged to hide behind these spikes to save themselves from some attacks the boss is doing. Visually making the teeth block the particle effects required us to go deeper in our use of Render Targets, so there was a lot of new ground covered there as well.

The logic handling the phases and intermissions also required making new systems for governing the boss’ actions on top of its regular behavior, to give the fight the structure we envisioned.

But beyond all that, a boss fight like The Prophet of Decay is a really exciting project for us because it truly involves every single development craft on Darktide to work together on one thing to get every part of it just right. Game designers and coders implementing the enemy, level designers and artists preparing the boss arena and how it interacts with the boss’ hazards, story writers crafting Rodin Karnak’s narrative, Voice Over work, visual effects, sound effects, character artists and animators bringing the Prophet to life… And of course, the music!

“I think you have all the disciplines here, so it’s been really exciting.” ~ Jonathan

Bonus Question: What was your favorite part about working on the Prophet of Decay?

“On a bigger scale, getting to make a new boss for Darktide. On a more micro level, it’s been very fun building the underlying mechanic we have to make the boss a reality. We have a layer that sits on top of the normal behavior of the enemy that decides the phases, and how to handle the whole fight structure, really.” ~ Jonathan


That’s all we have for today! We hope you enjoyed this deeper look into the Prophet of Decay boss fight and his design!

We’ll see you on the Mourningstar.

– The Darktide Team

item.title: Patch 9.0.3
item.description:
Hey folks,

We’ve just rolled out Patch 9.0.3, which brings with it:

  • Updates to Nagash’s campaign based on your valuable feedback.

  • Some tweaks to the Lords of the End Times factions to address some unintended behaviour.

  • Wider battle balancing changes to various Characters, Units and Spells, including Lore of Nehekhara.

  • A swathe of bug fixes and other adjustments, including:

    • Legendary Lords and Heroes confederated after their faction is destroyed now retain their Items and Ancillaries.

    • Nagash now has access to Unusual Locations and Ancillaries.

    • Styrkaar is now available to Norscan factions.

    • Warriors of Chaos can now continue recruiting after their Lord is defeated.

    • Fervour is now correctly awarded after fighting settlements defended by a garrisoned army.

    • Gotrek and Felix’s quest battle now resolves correctly.

Thank you to everyone for providing your bug reports and feedback on our forums and Reddit bug megathread. The work doesn’t slow down here, and the team are already looking into further fixes and changes for the next release which we’ll be rolling out as soon as we’re able.

As always, if you run into any new issues after updating to 9.0.3, please report them in our dedicated bug reporting sub-forum (and do include save files wherever possible - it helps massively!)

On to the notes…

Nagash Campaign Updates

Economy & Early Progression

Since release, we've been closely following your feedback and feel Nagash's economy still isn't hitting the right balance between challenge and enjoyment. These changes are aimed at easing early-game economic pressure by giving players more meaningful goals in the Black Pyramid, and increasing battle income on lower campaign difficulties.

  • Added -40% upkeep for Nagash to an early Black Pyramid node.

  • Added -10% upkeep to the early Tomb Kings, Vampire Coast, and Vampire Counts sections of the Black Pyramid. This only applies to units led by a matching lord type, or by Nagash himself.

  • Post-battle income now scales with campaign difficulty:

    • Legendary / Very Hard: No change

    • Hard: +5%

    • Normal: +10%

    • Easy: +20%

Sigil Progression

We also felt players weren't able to empower Sigils as quickly as intended, particularly in the early game. These changes increase early-game Sigil generation and make progression through the Black Pyramid happen at a more rewarding pace.

  • Increased the Legendary Lord subjugation bonus in the Mortarchs panel from 5 to 10 Sigils (Heroes and Nameless characters remain at 5).

  • Increased Sigils generated by Nagashizzar and the Black Pyramid of Nagash from 2/4/6/8/10 to 3/6/9/12/15.

  • Increased Sigils generated by standard Necropolises from 2/2/4/4/6 to 2/3/4/5/8.

  • Reduced the Necromancy Panel’s Sigil unlock requirement from 200 to 100 Necromantic Energy. This change will affect new campaigns.

Necropolises & Local Recruitment

We’ve implemented several changes to Necropolises, making developing them more valuable. One primary issue we wanted to address was that players weren’t feeling the need to build recruitment buildings anymore once they had started to unlock a few Grave Call options, so we are adding both local and global benefits to recruitment buildings that aim to keep them useful throughout the campaign.

  • Improved garrisons for standard Necropolises, Nagashizzar, the Black Pyramid of Nagash, and all Necropolis defence buildings.

  • Added combat bonuses for units under siege to the Necropolis Garrison chain when the province is devastated.

  • Added significant local recruitment cost reductions from military building chains while a province is devastated, making local recruitment a more attractive alternative to Grave Call.

  • Military building chains now grant -1% factionwide upkeep for their associated unit types while the province is devastated.

  • Corruption building chains now provide army movement bonuses in devastated provinces, spreading to adjacent provinces at the highest tier.

Mortarch & Confederation Objectives

One of the most consistent points of feedback we've received is that Mortarch subjugation objectives felt too restrictive and pushed players toward specific regions of the map.

Our goal is to give players greater freedom to expand where they want. In most cases, Mortarchs will now submit to Nagash's rule once he has clearly surpassed them in power, rather than requiring players to hunt them down across the map (however, doing so will speed up the process if they become too strong).

  • The "own a maximum of 5 regions" requirement for Mortarch Lords has been replaced. Nagash must now control more than three times as many regions as the Mortarch.

    • This change has also been applied to the Vampire Count confederation panel.

  • Most location-specific objectives, such as owning The Awakening or building the Blood Keep, have been removed and replaced with thematic objectives that can be completed from any location.

  • Legendary Hero objectives have been made easier, allowing earlier subjugation.

  • These new objectives will only apply to new campaigns, ensuring existing campaign progress isn't disrupted.

9.0.3 Release Notes

Performance & Stability

  • Fixed a crash that could occur when loading certain campaign save files.

  • Fixed a crash that could occur when using the Vampire Counts Confederation panel.

  • Fixed a crash that could occur when attempting the Scheme battle for Bretonnia & Athel Loren as the Changeling.

  • Fixed a crash that could occur upon the start of the Chaos Dwarf endgame crisis.

  • Fixed a crash that could occur after defeating Helman Ghorst in battle.

Campaign
General/Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue causing Nagash to not have access to Unusual Locations.

  • Fixed an issue causing Nagash to not have access to some Ancillaries.

  • Fixed an issue where Beastmen Lords were spawning with 1.4k weapon strength.

  • Styrkaar the Sortsvinaer is now available to all Norscan factions.

  • Fixed an issue where Warriors of Chaos were unable to recruit after their Lord was defeated.

  • Fixed an issue where the level of Vampiric Corruption was not correctly reducing the cost of Ritual of Undeath.

  • Fixed an issue where razing Skavenblight as Thanquol prevented the quest “Steal the Plan-Prints” from being completed.

  • Fixed an issue where the Clawmark Scribe would not gain experience when Thanquol gained a rank.

  • Fixed all cases where Corpses and Blood resources were refunding units for more than they were recruited for. This includes a revision of some sources of recruitment cost reductions into increasing Corpses from battle.

  • Fixed an issue where the Quest battle to acquire Gotrek and Felix would not end when all objectives were completed.

  • The Bone Giant unit is now available to all owners of the Nagash DLC, regardless of whether you own the Tomb Kings DLC.

  • Fixed an issue where mission objectives to control regions would show as not completed after a reload, even though they were.

  • Fixed an issue where cancelling building construction would sometimes not refund Necromantic Energy.

  • Fixed an issue where if Nagash subjugates a Mortarch that has a starting Hero, that Hero would be using Emil Valgeir’s model.

  • Fixed an issue where a player playing with a Mortarch faction might suddenly get confederated by Nagash.

  • Fixed an issue where Neferata was able to make peace with Khalida via regular diplomacy.

  • Fixed an issue where missions that require moving to a specific region would abort if that region’s owner was vassalised.

  • Fixed an issue where Vampire Coast factions could no longer trigger and benefit from battle site markers created after large battles.

  • Fixed an issue where new armies could spawn endlessly during the Chaos Dwarf endgame crisis.

Victory Conditions

  • Fixed an issue where Alarielle's long victory objective to control a Wood Elf settlement was not showing as completed despite controlling a Wood Elf settlement.

  • Fixed an issue where Dechala's Pleasure Palace long victory condition was not counting settlements converted to Palaces after capture.

  • Removed Arkhan the Black’s victory conditions “Hold the following settlement: Black Tower of Arkhan” and “Construct landmark: Black Tower of Arkhan”, and replaced them with "Control the following settlement either by direct ownership or through allies: Black Tower of Arkhan" to avoid having to go to war with Nagash to complete the objectives.

  • When playing as Teclis, if the player choses to return to Ulthuan the victory objective for short victory now requires the construction of a landmark in either Hoeth OR Fortress of Dawn.

Skills, Abilities & Traits

  • ​Fixed an issue where the Hounds of Ulricsberg (Hunting Hounds) Battle Howl ability was missing from Campaign.

  • Fixed an issue where Immortal Empires campaign Points of Interest pins were not displayed.

  • The Vampire Lair traits "The Commander" and "The Inflamed" no longer apply their negative effects to Lords and Heroes when the negative effect mentions "all units".

  • The Vampire Lair traits "The Undeafeated" and "The Commander" no longer apply their positive effects to Lords and Heroes when the positive effect mentions specific unit ranks.

Nagash Campaign Updates

Economy & Early Progression

Since release, we've been closely following your feedback and feel Nagash's economy still isn't hitting the right balance between challenge and enjoyment.   • Post-battle income now scales with campaign difficulty:

    • Legendary / Very Hard: No change

    • Hard: +5%

    • Normal: +10%

We’ve implemented several changes to Necropolises, making developing them more valuable. One of the most consistent points of feedback we've received is that Mortarch subjugation objectives felt too restrictive and pushed players toward specific regions of the map.

Our goal is to give players greater freedom to expand where they want.
